t: The corner post shifted while the wall settled. I need to reset it.
I cut that beam twice and it remains too short.
The new hinge swings cleanly without lifting the door.
Wet wood makes every joint lie about how well it fits.
I should brace the wall before adding weight above it.
A straight roof begins with posts nobody notices afterward.
The stew thickened while I was chopping the last roots.
I should skim that pot before the bitter taste spreads.
The grain cooked unevenly because the fire favored one side.
A covered pot needs less watching and somehow gets more.
The last bowl always finds somebody who arrived late.
Tomorrow I will start the broth before everyone begins asking about supper.
The ridge revealed another valley and three more days of walking.
I marked the path well enough to find it in rain.
The shallow crossing moved downstream after the last storm.
Every distant hill looks gentle until I begin climbing it.
I found smoke beyond the trees and no fire beneath it.
The return path needs marks facing home, not only outward.
The seedlings near the fence came up before the middle rows.
I buried that seed too deeply and knew it while doing it.
The soil is dry beneath the surface despite yesterday's rain.
Bird tracks cover the row I finished last.
I should mend the fence before blaming animals for entering.
One bad patch does not condemn the whole field.
The net came up heavy with weeds and one angry fish.
I should replace the frayed line before it costs a good catch.
The water cleared after the wind changed direction.
Fish took the bait near the bank and ignored the deeper hook.
The reeds hide every snag until the net finds it.
I can mend three small holes faster than one torn edge.
The trunk twisted after the first cut opened it.
I should clear the branches before somebody trips beneath the tree.
That stand looks healthy from the path and rotten from inside.
The bark came away easily where water reached the roots.
A dull axe makes every tree feel twice its size.
I left the younger trunks room to grow straight.
The red berries are ready, but the darker ones need time.
I found edible roots where the soil stays loose under leaves.
The smallest basket keeps me from crushing what lies beneath.
I should return before rain washes the scent from these herbs.
Someone picked the easy side and left the thorny work for me.
A patch can look empty until I kneel beside it.
The western fence has one gap wide enough for trouble.
I know every nighttime sound except the one I just heard.
The torch smokes whenever the wind drops.
People wave more often when they know I am watching.
I should walk the same route backward and see what I missed.
Quiet is good. Distrust of quiet keeps it that way.
The swelling is lower than yesterday, though the skin remains hot.
I need to boil more cloth before the next patient arrives.
That cough sounds shallow until they try to stand.
The cleanest wound often belongs to the person who complains most.
I should write nothing off as tiredness before checking the fever.
Rest is the treatment everyone agrees with and nobody follows.
The animal circled behind me after I thought the trail had ended.
I should smooth that rough shaft before it cuts my palm again.
Tracks near water tell less because every creature uses the same bank.
The birds warned the animal about me before I saw it.
A patient hour can save half a day of following.
I found the trail late enough to know where tomorrow begins.
The support sounds different after the wall has been opened.
I should wet the dust before it fills the whole passage.
The ore thinned exactly where the stone became easier.
My lamp showed a crack the brighter daylight somehow missed.
A good strike makes a sound worth remembering.
I need another pair of hands before moving that stone.
People confess small doubts after public certainty tires them.
I chose the wrong story for the mood in the room.
The same words comfort one person and irritate the next.
I should ask questions before turning every concern into instruction.
Someone always watches how I react before choosing their own reaction.
A quiet shrine still needs somebody present when trouble arrives.
My hands stopped working before the rest of me admitted it.
I have enough strength for one more task and no sense to choose it.
Sitting down was a mistake. Standing again will be worse.
Every tool feels heavier at the end of the day.
I should eat before tiredness turns into anger.
Tomorrow's work already feels unreasonable from here.
I have begun counting steps to the nearest place to sit.
The day is over. My shoulders have known for hours.
